Pulled from the Consent  Richard Bowen, La Verne  resident,  requested  that Resolution No. 19- 34,
Calendar/  approving annual agreements be pulled from the Consent Calendar for further
Resolution  No. 19- 34,  discussion.
Authorizing Annual City
Agreements  Once a year, the City Council  considers annual agreements for renewals or
  extensions.  As such,  attached are the services proposed for the coming fiscal
  year  for City Council  consideration.  A summary of the agreements which
  includes  purposes  of the  agreement,  cost changes  proposed (  if any) were  also

  included.

  Richard Bowen, La Verne resident stated that the Council should not approve
  the agreements.  He stated it was not right just to roll over the  agreements.  He
  asked how the City can know if they are getting the best price without going out
  to bid.  He stated it makes no sense and should  be part of the process to go out
  to bid.
  He also stated that there should be a no donation or gifts to City
  Employees and City Council clause.

  Steve Johnson, 2175 Third Street, La Verne  resident, stated that the City

  Council owes the residents to be fiscally responsible and that the City should go
  out  to bid and not just rolling over the agreements.  He stated we are in a
  competitive  environment  and  that the City can do better.  He spoke about
  Waste Management not being the only waste hauler and the City should go out
  to bid for the best deal.

  Richard Gil, La Verne stated that the Federal government never stays with the
  same  contractors  and  they always  to bid.
  He stated that the City should
  go out

  go out bid not to follow past practices of rolling over contracts.

  Public Works Director Keesey stated that each contract is carefully evaluated,
  vetted for the best price and services in the area and they are not just rolled
  over.  He stated that agreements  are inline or lower than what is found in other
  local agencies. He stated he has given his heart and soul to the City for the
  past 33 years and he is bothered by the lack of trust. He spoke about the
  importance of the  service,  response,  and knowledge which is as much or more
  important than  a  low bid.  He made reference to a water civil engineer who' s
  been with the City for over 30 years and helped build the City' s water system.
  He stated that his knowledge is invaluable, where it would take him an hour to
  evaluate  a problem,  with a new engineer  it could take  several  hours.
   City Council  Minutes,  Monday, June 3, 2019, Page 5

  City Manager Russi stated that per the City' s purchasing  policy, the Finance
  Department evaluates each agreement and works with each department to
  determine whether competitive bidding should be undertaken instead of
  renewal  and  that agreements  are  not  just rolled  over.  He stated that the San
  Gabriel Valley Council of Governments is looking at an economy scale on
  certain common service agreements to package together with other cities,
  which  may result in savings.  He stated  once  the survey is completed,  and if it
  results  in savings, he would  bring it to City Council for their consideration.

  Council Carder stated that of the twenty- two contracts only four showed an
  increase.

  Council Member Davis thanked Public Works Director Keesey for his remarks.
  He stated he believes in the staff and that they manage the City' s portfolio
  frugally and he is in support in approving the agreements.

  Mayor Pro Tem Rosales stated that the quality of service was important and he
  referred to the signal maintenance contractor who knows the City well and
  provides  the best price  and service.  He stated that there are things that Waste
  Management does not charge the City and it saves the City money.

  Council  Member  Hepburn  stated he valued the talents of Public Works Director
  Keesey  and  his service to the City, but that we are in a completive  bidding
  environment  and should  go out  to bid.  He stated that even if we went out to bid
  on the largest contracts it could save the City money.

  Mayor Kendrick stated that the City of La Verne is a frugally managed City. He
  stated that the Public Works Director carefully vets each agreement every year.
  City staff contacts other surrounding cities who contract with same contractors
  for comparison,  and that is like going out to bid.  He stated that Waste
  Management  is the third lowest of thirteen local haulers. He referred to the
  City' s top credit rating which shows how fiscally well managed the City is.

  It was moved  by Carder, seconded by Davis, and carried by vote of 4- 1,
  Hepburn No) to approve the  annual City Agreements  by adopting Resolution
  No. 19- 34, which authorizes the Mayor and Assistant City Clerk to execute
  the annual agreements as listed in the resolution.

9.  Los Angeles  County Feasibility  Mayor Kendrick  stated that Council  Member  Hepburn  requested  that the topic
  study for Providing Fire  of the  Los Angeles  County feasibility study for providing  fire  services  be
  Services Consideration  brought  back  before the City Council for consideration.  This request is
  consistent with the Council' s rules of reconsideration.

  Council Member Hepburn stated that he originally voted no when Council
  Member Davis brought this issue back in February, because he was
  concerned  with  Firefighters  lawsuit and it adding fuel to the fire.  He stated that
  now  that the lawsuits  are  resolved,  he felt it was the right time to do the free
  fire study.  He stated it was important to be in line with transparency to show
  the residents  what  the costs would be for county fire services  vs.  in- house.
  Council Member Hepburn made the motion to do the free Fire Feasibility Study
  withthe County of Los Angeles. Motion stood.

  Council Member Carder stated that La Verne residents want their own fire
  department and she did not support doing the fire study.

  Council Member Davis asked Council Member Hepburn why he was bringing
  back this matter for Council consideration  when he voted no to do the free
  study  when  City Council. He stated he was still
  he brought this before the
  open  to  doing the fire study,
  but he was puzzled as to the reason why Council
  Member Hepburn was bringing this matter back now.
   City Council Minutes, Monday, June 3, 2019, Page 7

  Mayor Pro Tem Rosales stated when this matter was originally heard by
  Council, he wanted to move forward with the free fire study because he
  thought  that is what the Fire Department wanted.  Since the lawsuits are in the
  rearview  mirror and  seeing the Fire Badge pinning tonight,  he cannot support

  doing a study at this time.

  City Manager Russi stated it would be beneficial to have the information of the
  fire study available when pursuing the tax measure.

  Mayor Kendrick stated he felt it would cost the City more if they went County
  and  it would affect the quality of life in the community. He stated that residents
  want  their own Fire Department with the current fire staff. He stated he was
  not  in favor in doing the study. He stated that the City should  pursue the tax
  measure  to get the sales tax, if not, the County will take it.

  It was moved by Hepburn, seconded by Davis, and motion failed by a vote of
  Rosales No) to do a free Fire Feasibility Study with the
  3/ 2 ( Kendrick, Carder&
  County of Los Angeles.
